The tangency equation gives the sharp cap threshold, and a separate global tangent identity handles m≤√(KI) with no cap; weak limits plus impossibility of equality give the unbounded-cap nonattainment statements. The treatment explicitly assumes exogenous concentration distributions and not feasible reactor controls.

originality.rationale: The general concave-envelope principle and Haldane kinetics are explicitly recognized as prior knowledge. The specific claim is the complete closed-form mean-cap optimizer and lower bound for arbitrary substrate distributions, the cap-to-mean transition B_c(m), unique two-point supports, and unattained no-cap extrema. Real searches of indexed mathematical results and the current ledger did not find a dominating implication; inspected full open texts concern cultivation process or dynamically constrained buffered chemostats, and distinct scope is shown. Publisher-abstract-only sources do not justify whole-document absence; their historical-priority risk is retained. Independent priority confirmation is not claimed.
residual_risks: Older physical-bioprocess or convex-optimization literature might already contain an equivalent exact Haldane concave-envelope calculation under different terminology.
Andrews 1968 and Bayen–Rapaport–Tani 2020 were not obtained in full; abstract-only scope comparison is not a full-text exclusion.
The occupation law may not be physically realizable under nutrient mass conservation or bounded feed-rate controls; the mathematical theorem deliberately does not imply such realizability.

value.rationale: Substrate-inhibition and pulsed high-cell-density cultivation naturally raise the nontrivial question of when a given mean input should be distributed in time rather than held constant, under an upper toxicity bound. This theorem solves the entire all-Borel-law problem, including unique support and weights, the biologically interpretable phase boundary of when variability helps, a sharp lower bound, and a singular high-cap limit; none is merely an arbitrary slice or a minor numeric improvement. It gives a useful theoretical ceiling and potential falsification benchmark for any physically constrained feeding policy, while clearly separating exogenous concentration schedules from actual controls.
